source: NCERT Class X, Understanding Economic Development, Economics Ch. 2.

sections.heading: 1. Three Sectors of the Economy
points: **Primary (agricultural) sector** — produces goods by exploiting **natural resources** (agriculture, dairy, fishing, forestry, mining).
**Secondary (industrial) sector** — transforms raw materials into **manufactured goods** (factories, industry).
**Tertiary (service) sector** — provides **services** that support the other two (transport, banking, trade, communication, education, health, IT).

sections.heading: 2. Comparing Sectors — GDP and Employment
points: **GDP** = value of all **final goods and services** produced in a country in a year; the sum of production in the three sectors.
Historical shift: primary → secondary → **tertiary** as countries develop.
In India, the **tertiary sector is now the largest producer** (share of GDP), but **most people are still employed in agriculture** — a mismatch.
**Disguised (hidden) unemployment** — more people work on a farm/shop than actually needed; removing some would not reduce output.
Reasons for tertiary sector growth: basic services (govt), development of agriculture/industry, rising incomes, and new services like **IT**.

sections.heading: 3. Organised vs Unorganised Sector
points: **Organised sector** — registered, fixed hours, regular employment, job security, benefits (PF, paid leave, pension) — governed by rules/laws.
**Unorganised sector** — small, scattered units outside government control; **low pay, no security, no benefits, irregular work** (small shops, casual labour, small farmers).
Most workers in India are in the **unorganised sector**; they need **protection and support** (registration, minimum wages, welfare).

sections.heading: 4. Public vs Private Sector, and MGNREGA
points: **Public sector** — government owns assets and provides services (railways, post); aims at people's welfare, not just profit.
**Private sector** — owned by individuals/companies; profit motive.
**Right to Work — MGNREGA (2005)** guarantees **100 days of wage employment** a year to rural households; if not provided, an **unemployment allowance** is paid — helps reduce disguised unemployment.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Primary = natural resources; Secondary = manufacturing; Tertiary = services.
GDP = value of all final goods and services in a year.
India: tertiary = largest in GDP, but agriculture employs the most (disguised unemployment).
Organised = registered + secure + benefits; Unorganised = insecure, low-paid.
MGNREGA (2005) = 100 days guaranteed rural employment (Right to Work).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Mining is in the primary sector** (exploits nature), not secondary.
**GDP** counts only **final** goods and services (avoid double counting).
**Disguised unemployment** = more workers than needed (common in agriculture).
**MGNREGA** guarantees **100 days** of employment (Right to Work, 2005).
